Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test case attempts to select an option with only a long name (no short opt) within an OptionGroup and asserts that this option is selected. The bug report explains that when the option lacks a short name, the selection mechanism fails because group.setSelected(option) has no effect.

Looking at OptionGroup.setSelected(Option), the key logic is:
- If selected is null or selected equals option.getOpt(), then selected is set to option.getOpt().
- Otherwise, an AlreadySelectedException is thrown.

Here, selected and option.getOpt() represent the selected option by its short name (opt). The problem is that if option.getOpt() returns null (which happens if the option only has a long name and no short name), then selected is set to null or comparisons are made against null, which breaks the logic. Indeed, Option.getOpt() returns the short option string, which may be null.

In contrast, OptionGroup stores options by key using option.getKey(), which returns longOpt if opt is null (short opt). However, in setSelected, it relies on option.getOpt() which does not account for long options without short names.

Thus, the core issue is inconsistency in using getOpt() versus getKey() for identifying the selected option in OptionGroup. The OptionGroup.addOption method correctly uses getKey() as the map key, but setSelected wrongly uses getOpt(). This means setting a selected option without short opt results in no actual selection.

Therefore, the bug arises because OptionGroup.setSelected uses option.getOpt() (short name) which can be null and fails for options that only have a long name.

To fix this, OptionGroup.setSelected should use option.getKey() when setting the selected option to handle both short and long option names uniformly. This change would allow selecting options that only have long names and no short names.

No need to inspect parsing logic further, as the bug is clearly in the OptionGroup's selection tracking.

Summary:
- OptionGroup options stored by key with getKey()
- OptionGroup.setSelected uses getOpt() which can be null
- This causes failure to track selected options without short names
- Fix by using getKey() in setSelected instead of getOpt()
